data.name: Element4l
data.detailed_description:
Element4l é um jogo de plataforma indie experimental, com um forte foco em fluxo e suavidade na jogabilidade, envolto em uma trilha sonora excepcional pela Mind Tree.

Em Element4l, você controla 4 elementos que estão unidos em uma jornada para formar a vida. Seus únicos obstáculos são a Natureza e o Sol. Ele tem uma abordagem diferente e inovadora para jogos de plataforma clássicos e desafia você a reordenar seus reflexos.

Element4l é um desafio. A primeira vez em que jogar, você vai se esforçar... Assim como a primeira vez em que aprendeu a andar de bicicleta.

--- Características ---

  • Elementos com movimentos ninja.
  • Jogabilidade baseada em 4 botões alternativos.
  • Trilha sonora excepcional pela Mind Tree (incluído gratuitamente com alta qualidade MP3).
  • 16 níveis ao todo, em 4 etapas (+ níveis de tutorial e bônus).
  • Modo de corrida competitiva com adaptação Ghost de outros jogadores.
  • Colecionáveis / realizações / ovos de páscoa /...
  • Expansão ""Modo Corrida"" gratuita incluída.

reviews.review:
FOUR ELEMENTS, ZERO CONTROL, AND ONE VERY ANGRY PLAYER!

Oh, for fck's sake. ELEMENT4L, WHAT THE ACTUAL HELL ARE YOU EXPECTING ME TO DO HERE?

I came here to play a platformer, not enroll in an advanced degree in fcking elemental physics taught by a suicidal physics professor. At first glance, the game actually looks pretty damn appealing. It's visually interesting, the concept seems creative, and the idea of controlling different elements to navigate through a world sounds like it could lead to some genuinely entertaining gameplay. 

AND THEN YOU ACTUALLY TOUCH THE CONTROLS.

Suddenly, you're not playing a video game anymore. You're participating in a government-funded experiment to determine how long a human being can tolerate complete bullshit before their brain files for divorce. Let's examine our four magnificent elemental bastards: 

🔥 FIRE: Touch something, explode. Touch something else, probably explode. Breathe incorrectly, fucking explode. Congratulations, you're now a firework with commitment issues.

💨 AIR: Apparently, this motherfucker also explodes on contact. What kind of air is this? Chernobyl air? Concentrated bullshit in gaseous form? I thought air was supposed to help things move, not turn me into a goddamn environmental hazard.

🧊 ICE: This slippery little shit sends you sliding for several metres before suddenly deciding that forward momentum is a myth invented by Big Physics. You spend half your time sliding uncontrollably and the other half wondering whether your character has brakes or whether they're just decorative.

🪨 STONE: And then there's stone. What the fuck does stone even do? I genuinely don't know. It's sitting there like that one employee in an office who attends every meeting, contributes absolutely nothing, and somehow still gets paid.

FOUR ELEMENTS. FOUR PERSONALITY DISORDERS. ABSOLUTELY NO COOPERATION.

And the worst part isn't even that the game is difficult. Difficult games can be fantastic. I enjoy a challenge. I enjoy learning mechanics, mastering controls, and overcoming obstacles that initially seem impossible. But there's a difference between a game challenging your skills and a game making you question whether the controls were designed by someone who has never actually played a fucking video game. Here, simply moving forward becomes an exercise in trial and error. You have to figure out which element to use, when to switch, how long to hold it, and what combination of button presses might prevent your character from immediately transforming into a spectacular elemental disaster. 

And when you fail? You try again. And fail again. And again. Eventually, you're no longer thinking strategically. You're just throwing random combinations of elemental bullshit at the screen and praying that the game decides to cooperate for approximately three seconds. THIS ISN'T PLATFORMING. THIS IS ELEMENTAL ROULETTE. 

The game wants you to understand the relationship between its elements, but the experience is so confusing and frustrating that I have absolutely no desire to experiment with them. Every new attempt feels less like I'm learning a clever mechanic and more like I'm trying to operate a malfunctioning washing machine without the instruction manual. And that's a massive problem, because a game built entirely around unique movement mechanics NEEDS those mechanics to feel intuitive enough that players actually want to master them. If moving your character is already an exhausting chore, why the fuck would I care about reaching the next level? The visuals might grab your attention for a few seconds, and the concept might initially seem promising, but pretty graphics can only carry a game so far. Eventually, someone has to make the actual gameplay enjoyable. ELEMENT4L APPARENTLY FORGOT THAT PART. I wanted to explore the game. Instead, I spent my time fighting its controls. I wanted to progress through the levels. Instead, I got stuck playing an endless game of "Which Elemental Bastard Do I Activate Before Everything Goes Wrong?" And after enough of that nonsense, the frustration completely overwhelms whatever enjoyment the game might have offered. 

FOUR ELEMENTS, INFINITE FRUSTRATION. Element4l might have an interesting concept and some appealing visuals, but the controls make the entire experience intolerable for me. When simply moving forward requires an endless cycle of confusing switches, accidental explosions, uncontrollable sliding, and blind trial and error, I have absolutely no motivation to continue. I don't want to spend my evening conducting elemental research just to move five fucking metres. I wanted to play a game, not become the world's most underpaid intern at the Department of Fire, Ice, Air, and Unexplained Stone. 

Abandon this game Emotionally, spiritually, and elementally.
